articles.title: The profile of adults diagnosed with autism has shifted markedly since 2010
articles.summary: Since 2010, the profile of newly diagnosed autistic adults in the UK and Sweden has shifted markedly. Rates have climbed fastest among women and young adults, alongside rising histories of anxiety, depression, and ADHD.

articles.title: Impressionist beauty ideals aligned with modern clinical classifications of obesity
articles.summary: By using artificial intelligence to estimate the body mass index of female figures in 19th-century paintings, researchers reveal how historical ideals of beauty contrast starkly with today’s demands for extreme thinness.

articles.title: Dopamine cells slow the heart during danger, new fruit fly research indicates
articles.summary: Four dopamine-producing brain cells slow a fruit fly’s heartbeat when a puff of air startles it. The same cells also drive the fly to walk more, linking threat detection to both heart and legs.

articles.title: Eating more fruits and vegetables is linked to a lower risk of depression
articles.summary: Eating more fruits and vegetables is consistently linked to a lower risk of depression, according to a massive new review of observational studies. Researchers found that every additional 200 grams of daily produce corresponds to better mental health outcomes.

articles.title: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
articles.summary: A revolutionary new wearable patch could help people get more restorative sleep without medication or surgery. Developed by University of Texas researchers, the device uses gentle ultrasound to stimulate deep brain regions, helping participants enter REM sleep 43 minutes faster and remain there 16 minutes longer on average. The technology also showed promising effects on stress regulation and brain circuits involved in emotion.

articles.title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
articles.summary: New research reveals that biological sex, genetics, and menopause may dramatically influence Alzheimer's risk, treatment responses, and chronic pain conditions such as fibromyalgia. Scientists also uncovered surprising differences in immune activity and gut-brain interactions, opening the door to more personalized treatments for neurological disorders.

articles.title: MIT scientists discover a surprising way to boost the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
articles.summary: MIT scientists discovered that carefully timed bursts of gentle pink noise during sleep can strengthen the brain’s natural cleaning waves, which help flush away potentially harmful waste. The breakthrough could pave the way for new treatments aimed at improving sleep and memory while potentially reducing the buildup of proteins linked to Alzheimer’s disease.

articles.title: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
articles.summary: A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago may have helped shape one of the most important differences between humans and our closest relatives: how our brains develop. Scientists at Lund University discovered that ancient viral DNA embedded in the chimpanzee genome switches off a gene called LINC00662, which remains active in humans and appears to play an important role in early brain development.

articles.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. We show that this hard-filtering step can reduce downstream accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts. Across three models, a controlled sensitivity intervention moves hard-drop from gains of +0.186 to +0.230 at perfect resolution to losses of -0.176 to -0.181 at the lowest tested reliability. Paired targeted interventions show that false-drop causes significantly greater degradation than false-keep, while a non-deleting baseline can still fail when incorrect labels steer

articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Connecting microscopic neuronal spiking to macroscopic brain function is a central challenge in computational neuroscience.
